notes: The original execution made no commit; its backend work was subsequently committed through 4075a54. E-196 through E-203 describe later uncommitted work. E-204 is a status-only reconciliation and creates no code commit or release.
The 2026-10-31 B3 verified image was observed on authorized standby PID 46568; this is a dated observation, not a claim about the current process or later source deployment.

E-196 records 29 interaction cases; E-198 adds UI-30 and E-203 retains 30/30, layout 11 surfaces / 70 controls and overflow 9 areas. These are prior scoped runs, not tests re-executed by E-204. The read-only source still awaits real desktop/8788 acceptance. Per-attempt model/day reconciliation remains master-plan work.

Imported history is stored in schema-v5 tables, keyed by source, instance and entity id; cc-switch and Claude Code adapters have fixture evidence. The initial schema-4 refusal described in E-197 was superseded by E-203: schemas 4-5 are accepted read-only without migration.

History sources are discovered by existence only — CC Switch's cc-switch.db in its conventional directories, Claude Code's projects folder when it holds a transcript — and a successfully previewed path is remembered in import-sources.json (five newest, atomic write, corrupt file means nothing remembered). Discovery and memory are verified against temporary roots, not a real installation, and never read a database or transcript.

The first real-looking import exposed two defects that fixtures had hidden: the cc-switch day rollup stores AVG(latency_ms) as REAL and the reader demanded INTEGER, and a client record written before the desktop rule stored raw user-agent text as its display name. The reader now accepts either numeric type (with a REAL regression fixture) and the per-client ledger looks the name up at aggregation, leaving the stored record, family and confidence unchanged.

The imported period is read from the store's own earliest counted day, not from the first row of the windowed day list: an import older than the chart window still moves the period, and a suspected duplicate does not get to claim it.

Imported history is part of this device's history, so the Activity headline and day curve carry both stores: the additive counters and known spend are summed and `since` moves back, while the client/model split and attribution remain the live ledger's own and say so — the imported store has no request kind or attribution evidence, and fabricating either would make the split disagree with the headline. The read-only standby opener accepts schema 4 through 5 because v5 only added the imported tables; older layouts still need their owning build.

E-204 source review narrows the multi-currency claim: both imported_totals and imported_days currently sum cost_usd; other currencies survive only in the stored fact JSON. Unified non-USD headline/chart/export accounting and cross-source identity remain incomplete. B5 SQL history paging exists in the backend but Activity still pages its recent window; B6 file export is already connected.
